idiom_name: dict access with .get(key, default) / dataclass field defaults (pydantic extra='ignore' for structured readers)
implementation_notes: JSON decodes to plain dict/list, so the simpler local idiom replaces the classic reader class entirely: a small function maps the dict to your own type, reading required fields with payload["x"] (fail fast, KeyError) and optional ones with payload.get("x", default), which ignores everything else by construction because the payload is never validated as a whole. Dataclass field defaults supply the missing-value half for free, and pydantic is the structured variant - its models ignore undeclared keys by default (ConfigDict extra='ignore'), so producer additions never reach the model.
pitfalls: dict.get swallows typos: a producer rename yields the default silently instead of an error, so the reader must log or assert when a consumed key disappears.
An explicit JSON null becomes None, so .get("x", default) can still return None; use `"x" not in payload` when absent and null must be distinguished.
Read-only discipline matters: handing the raw dict to the rest of the system lets later code mutate the payload or read keys ad hoc, reintroducing the coupling the reader was meant to remove.
